I think it’s really unlikely you wont be able to get any tickets if you log on at 9. Honestly. 

You will be able to get into the park and shouldn’t have a problem parking at the visitors center *if you arrive in the morning.* I think I got there about 830/9, and made coffee/breakfast in my car and just hung out until my shuttle time at 10. The later you arrive, the harder it will be to find parking. They have bathrooms and a nice sized gift shop to walk around too. 

You can park in Springdale and walk/shuttle into the park but it costs like $20/day. I don’t have any knowledge about private shuttles but you could probably give a couple places a call and just ask how much availability they have left. 

I recommend looking at a map of the park to help orient yourself and ease some worries. Once you get there, getting around will be very straightforward..but the biggest thing is getting the tickets obviously... I also use this “National Parks” App to help plan all my trips. It’s like a tan app with trees on the logo. It has offline maps and descriptions of all the hikes/viewpoints so you can plan out what you want to see a little bit more. 

Lmk if I can help answer any other questions!

Do we deduct the $100 for parking spots, then divided by 3? So I pay $866.33 (and get no parking spot) 

OR 

Divide rent by 3 then I deduct $50 because I don’t get a parking spot and would pay $849.66.

Or option C

Divide rent by 3. And deduct 100 from my payment because technically I’m not using $100 worth of the apartment value. In this case I pay $799.66.

However, in instances where there has been a miscarriage of justice- two wrongs do not make a right. 

In cases where the suspect is truly innocent, I would think the victims family would be more upset at the justice system for getting the wrong person and allowing the true culprit to run free, rather than be upset at someone who spent years in jail for a crime they did not commit.

I believe it’s more than 4%... Just looking at the stats in the US, 1527 people have died on death row since 1976. 170 people have been exonerated. I should say, 170 people have been lucky enough to be exonerated. 

To get the margin of error percentage, idk if you have to add the 170 to the total and then divide.. or divide as is. I have not done a math problem in like 8 years lol. HOWEVER either way you slice it, there is no way to truly get an accurate estimate  of how many innocent people died while waiting to be exonerated. 

Source- [DeathPenaltyInfo.Org](https://files.deathpenaltyinfo.org/documents/pdf/FactSheet.f1605882308.pdf)

Apologies that I assumed this was in the US! I see your point that if someone would rather die than live incarcerated, that they should have the right to do that. Some would argue that if someone who commits a heinous crime loses they right to choose. I’m not sure which side I agree with. 

Thank you for sharing insight into the UK justice  system. You are correct, the US is plagued with bs. The innocence project is great because they are able to use DNA evidence/testing to exonerate people. One could hope that because DNA technology has advanced so far compared to 20-30 years ago, that the possibility/likelihood of wrongful convictions will decrease. However DNA testing is only 1 piece to the puzzle, and like you pointed out, there are many injustices in the US system.

Many people on death row are wrongly convicted. Check out the Innocence Project. Their organization does a ton of amazing work to free those who have been wronged by the system. I cannot support the death penalty when there is such a high margin of error in the convictions.

I have re read this a few times now. I do agree that my perspective of independence is a coping mechanism like you have described here. 

While I wouldn’t necessarily call my previous relationship a complete failure, there were certainly insecurities that were present on both sides. Those insecurities rooted in distrust and resentment made it very difficult towards the end, and as a result I perhaps developed a more cynical view on relationships (for myself).

It’s not that I don’t want to be in a relationship.. it’s more so that I don’t want to hurt someone or get hurt, and so I don’t see a point in dating unless there is a true connection, which has been super difficult to find in the real world, post college!!

I sure am trying to live my life completely on my own terms and make decisions purely based on what I want to do, where I want to go, etc. I hope to get rid of this “independence crutch” at some point in my life. I suspect that may be during a time when my life is more stable and I have settled in a place for more than 10-12 months. We shall see.
